messages:
Dana: Weird one  set up the new aquarium LED strip near my desk and suddenly my wifi turns into a 90s dial-up impression. Photo: https://images.redwood.example/dana-aqua-led.jpg :fish: :bulb:

Miguel: lol electric fish startup kit? LEDs can introduce interference if they're cheap drivers. Any packet loss or just lag?

Dana: Both. Video stutters and my SSH session had a couple of freezes. Ran a quick ping while the light was on and saw this:

Dana: ```
$ ping -c 6 1.1.1.1
PING 1.1.1.1 (1.1.1.1): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=57 time=9.8 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=2 ttl=57 time=205.4 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=3 ttl=57 time=10.4 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=4 ttl=57 time=12.1 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=5 ttl=57 time=482.6 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=6 ttl=57 time=11.0 ms
--- 1.1.1.1 ping statistics ---
6 packets transmitted, 6 packets received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 9.8/121.9/482.6 ms
```

Priya: Those spikes smell like EMI from the LED driver or a shared outlet causing brief broadband noise. Try turning the strips off and see if it clears. Also try moving the router a bit further from the lights.

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: observed dana-laptop intermittent RTT spikes at 2412345750; peak RTT 483ms, 3 retransmits in last 15m. Suggested actions: power-cycle LED driver, move AP >30cm from high-power electronics, or test on a different outlet.

Yvonne: I had a similar issue with grow-lights. Cheap drivers are the worst. Ferrite bead on the LED power cable helped me. Also try a different power strip or plug into a different circuit.

Miguel: Quick A/B: put the LEDs on a surge strip with EMI filter or just unplug them during meetings to confirm. If it disappears, it's definitely the lights. Also moving to 5GHz often reduces this because 2.4GHz is more susceptible to overlapping noise.

Dana: Quick test done  unplugged LEDs and re-ran ping:

Dana: ```
$ ping -c 6 1.1.1.1
PING 1.1.1.1 (1.1.1.1): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=57 time=10.2 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=2 ttl=57 time=11.0 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=3 ttl=57 time=9.9 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=4 ttl=57 time=10.1 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=5 ttl=57 time=10.4 ms
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=6 ttl=57 time=10.0 ms
--- 1.1.1.1 ping statistics ---
6 packets transmitted, 6 packets received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max = 9.9/10.3/11.0 ms
```

Dana: Unplugged LEDs = stable. Plugged back in = spikes again. Guess the fish and my Zoom calls can't be friends. :fishy: :no_good:

Priya: Good repro. Options: swap to a higher-quality driver, add ferrite on the LED cable, plug LED into a different circuit, or move the router farther away. If you post the LED model folks can chime in.

Miguel: Name suggestion: "AquaLag" vs "FishNet". Vote with reactions. GIFs of dramatic fish protests accepted.

Dana: Ordered a ferrite clamp and switched the LED driver to a different outlet on another circuit. Will test during tomorrow's retro and report back. Thanks for the quick triage team. :heart:

Tooling Bot: network-monitor: after device moved at 2412345898 no retransmits observed in last 5m. Monitoring continues.

Yvonne: Love it. Bonus points for using an aquarium to justify more RGB expense. :tada:
